description:
Redwood Inference is running a Reliability Program focused on reducing incident frequency and improving MTTR via clearer ownership, consistent classification, and better tooling. This project—"Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping"—defines a standardized incident taxonomy (top incident types and subtypes), maps each type to a primary owning team/service, and establishes remediation SLAs (time-to-mitigate and time-to-fix expectations) by severity/tier (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

Goals:
- Produce a v1 incident taxonomy that is easy for on-call engineers to apply during live incidents and consistent enough for reporting.
- Map each incident type to a single primary owner (with secondary/consulted teams) and define escalation rules.
- Define remediation SLAs per incident type and severity, aligned with customer commitments and internal SLO/error budget policy.
- Integrate taxonomy + ownership into incident tooling (incident-bot, postmortem templates, dashboards, alerts) so classification is required, auditable, and measurable.
- Create reporting that shows incident volume, impact, and SLA compliance by type/owner to drive incident reduction work.

Scope:
- In-scope incident classes: availability (5xx/overload), latency regressions, streaming disconnects, routing/fallback misbehavior, capacity/fleet shortages, control plane outages, auth/RBAC failures, telemetry/metrics blind spots, and private deployment connectivity/config issues.
- Includes both customer-impacting incidents and high-severity internal incidents that threaten reliability.
- Out-of-scope for v1: deep root-cause frameworks (kept in postmortems), long-term product roadmap changes not tied to incident reduction.

Stakeholders and teams:
- Core: SRE (program lead, standards, dashboards), Platform Control Plane + Smart Routing (ownership mapping for routing/config), Infra/Fleet (capacity- and region-related types), Observability (metrics/cardinality/dashboards), Serving Runtime (runtime regression types), Security Ops (security incident alignment), Support/CS (customer comms + escalation mapping), Product (alignment with SLA commitments and Console surfacing).

Phases and timeline (typical 6–10 weeks):
1) Discovery + data pull: analyze recent incidents and support escalations; propose top 10–15 categories.
2) Taxonomy workshop(s): converge on definitions, decision tree, and examples.
3) Ownership + SLA alignment: validate owners with EMs/Directors; align remediation SLAs with customer tiers and incident process.
4) Tooling integration: incident-bot required fields, control-plane config for owner mapping, metrics labels, dashboards/alerts, and postmortem template updates.
5) Rollout + training: on-call playbook updates, announcements, office hours; enforce required classification; measure compliance.

Key constraints:
- Keep taxonomy low-cardinality and stable (avoid exploding label cardinality in metrics).
- Owners must be accountable and match real operational control boundaries.
- Remediation SLAs must be realistic given fleet constraints and release processes, while still driving meaningful improvement.

Primary deliverables:
- Confluence: published taxonomy definitions + decision tree, ownership mapping table, remediation SLA matrix, incident-process policy updates, ADR.
- Linear: implementation and rollout work items with dependencies.
- GitHub: PRs across incident-bot, redwood (instrumentation/control plane), observability-pack, slo-toolkit, docs.
- Slack: decision threads, rollout comms, live incident classification examples.
- Drive: working spreadsheets/analysis and workshop notes.
- Jira: representative support tickets linked back to taxonomy categories for validation.
- Fireflies: workshop transcript and select customer post-incident reviews used to validate comms + SLA alignment.

files.description: Program kickoff page: objectives, non-goals, scope (what counts as an incident type), initial stakeholders, working cadence, and success metrics (classification compliance, reporting coverage, incident reduction targets).
The v1 taxonomy: incident types/subtypes, definitions, inclusion/exclusion criteria, example symptoms, and a quick decision tree for on-call classification.
Owner mapping table (primary/secondary/consulted) by incident type + service, plus remediation SLAs by severity and customer tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with escalation rules.
Update to incident process: when classification is required, who sets/updates incident_type during an incident, what to do if unknown, and enforcement (cannot close without type/owner).
Postmortem template update: required fields for incident_type/subtype, owner, contributing systems, remediation SLA outcome, and links to dashboards; includes examples of good vs bad classification.
ADR documenting the decision to make incident taxonomy a required field across incident tooling, rationale, alternatives considered (freeform tags, service-only), and rollout plan.
Dashboard/alert spec: panels for incident volume by type/owner, MTTA/MTTR, SLA breach rate, top recurring types; includes data sources, metric names, and cardinality constraints.
How incident types map to SLOs/error budgets (availability vs latency), how incidents are counted, and how taxonomy enables error-budget burn breakdown and prioritization.
CS/Support guidance: how to communicate incident type to customers, which types require proactive outreach, templates for Dedicated/Private comms, and handoff points to SRE/on-call.
Runbook updates focusing on region failover and fleet capacity incidents: classification guidance, owner mapping (Fleet vs Routing vs Network), and standard mitigations.
Runtime-focused taxonomy appendix: common runtime regression patterns (OOM/kv-cache thrash/scheduler stalls), how they appear in symptoms/metrics, and the recommended taxonomy classification.
Alignment doc between reliability incident taxonomy and security incident categories: boundaries, handoff triggers, dual-tracking rules, and audit log expectations.
Linear ticket to draft and socialize the v1 taxonomy: links to Drive analysis, workshop agenda, reviewers, and acceptance criteria (bounded set, examples, decision tree).
Implement required incident_type/subtype fields in incident-bot, plus owner resolution (lookup table) and validation before incident can be marked resolved/closed.
Plumb incident_type through alert payloads and paging logic so pages route to the primary owner team when appropriate; includes fallback rules when type is unknown.
Add structured fallback_reason signals (capacity, health, policy, timeout) and map them to taxonomy classifications to reduce ambiguity during routing-related incidents.
Create a control-plane-managed config for ownership mapping (versioned, reviewed, auditable), with safe rollout/rollback and change log.
Add incident_type label to key error/latency metrics with strict cardinality controls and sampling rules; includes observability review.
One-time analysis/backfill task: classify recent incidents (from incident-bot + postmortems) into v1 taxonomy to validate top categories and baseline metrics.
Create and publish dashboards described in the Confluence spec; verify data accuracy; add saved views per tier/team.
Implement remediation SLA timers (by severity/type) and breach alerts; document how to pause/override during force majeure or customer-caused incidents.
PM work item to validate remediation SLAs against customer-facing commitments for Dedicated/Private, including edge cases (region-wide events, cloud provider outages).
Product ticket to surface incident type/owner in internal Console views (ops-only) and define what’s safe to expose to CS for customer comms.
Design exploration for Console/ops dashboards: filters, taxonomy drilldowns, and how to prevent misinterpretation (e.g., unknown/unclassified buckets).
Design templates for incident comms snippets (status page + email) keyed by incident type, focusing on clarity and avoiding over-specific root cause statements.
PR adding incident_type fields to internal alert payload schemas and incident creation endpoints; includes migration notes and tests.
PR introducing structured fallback_reason enums in routing, with mapping notes to taxonomy categories and metrics emitted for analysis.
PR adding a versioned owner-mapping configuration in the control plane, including validation, audit logging, and rollout safeguards.
PR extending internal APIs used by Console/ops to return incident_type, subtype, and resolved owner; includes permission checks.
PR adding incident_type labels to key reliability metrics and logs with cardinality guardrails; includes observability review comments.
PR wiring incident-bot output into runbook link suggestions based on incident type (e.g., overload vs auth vs routing).
PR adding a backfill job/pipeline that infers incident type from logs/annotations for historical reporting; includes accuracy caveats.
PR implementing remediation SLA timers and a breach alert (Slack + paging) keyed by severity/tier; includes configuration defaults.
PR updating on-call incident checklist templates in-repo (if applicable) to require taxonomy selection and owner confirmation.
PR updating incident-bot UX/commands to require incident_type/subtype, then auto-resolve owner team and suggest escalation channel.
PR adding heuristics to suggest a likely incident type from symptoms (5xx spike, p95 latency, streaming resets, capacity alerts), with override support.
PR enforcing closure gating: must include owner, incident type, and (for Sev0/Sev1) a postmortem link or placeholder ticket.
PR adding new dashboards and alert rules that break down incidents by taxonomy categories and owning team; includes playbook links.
Follow-up PR adjusting metric labeling/sampling to reduce cardinality risk, including guidance for unknown/unclassified buckets.
PR adding a small library/tool to compute remediation SLA due times and evaluate breaches based on incident severity, tier, and type.
Docs PR describing incident_type fields, how to classify during an incident, and how CS should interpret taxonomy in dashboards.
PR adding a perf-canary/synthetic test that exercises graceful degradation paths (fallback model/region) and emits signals used in taxonomy-related incidents.
Thread coordinating the initial taxonomy draft: proposed top-level categories, concerns about ambiguity, and agreement on keeping v1 small.
Thread reviewing a draft ownership mapping table; debate about whether routing vs fleet owns certain overload cases.
Thread about remediation SLAs: what’s realistic for Sev1 in Dedicated; discussion of cloud-provider outage carve-outs.
Thread with Observability engineers flagging metric label cardinality risks and suggesting an allowlist approach.
Thread planning the taxonomy workshop agenda and pre-read links (Drive spreadsheet + Confluence draft).
Thread announcing the policy: incident_type required in incident-bot for new incidents starting next week; Q&A from on-call.
Thread reviewing early adoption metrics: % classified, top unknown reasons, and action items to improve decision tree clarity.
Thread triaging edge cases: multi-cause incidents (capacity + routing) and rules for choosing primary type vs contributing factors.
Live incident coordination where the incident commander asks for taxonomy classification; discussion of whether it’s routing fallback misbehavior or capacity shortage.
Thread with incident-bot updates and a proposed incident_type; includes quick links to dashboards and runbooks.
Thread during a latency regression: deciding between runtime regression vs telemetry false positive; ends with tentative classification and next steps.
Thread after a streaming disconnect spike; on-call asks how to classify (client/network vs gateway) and who owns mitigation.
Thread involving Fleet and Routing during a regional capacity event; classification debate and owner assignment captured for postmortem.
Thread where security ops joins due to suspicious auth failures; notes on when to dual-track as security incident vs reliability incident.
Thread coordinating rollback and defining incident type for a control-plane outage; includes a note about SLA timer start/stop.
Thread summarizing incident closure gating in incident-bot (must set type/owner); on-call requests a temporary override for one case.
Thread discussing implementation details for owner mapping config in control plane: versioning, audit, and change review.
Thread about exposing incident_type in internal APIs and permissioning so CS can view but not modify.
Thread reporting a bug where owner resolution returns the wrong team for a subtype; quick patch coordination.
Thread coordinating rollout of the owner mapping config update; includes canary plan and monitoring checklist.
Thread on runtime regression classification examples: scheduler stalls vs KV cache thrash; agrees on mapping to specific subtypes.
Thread about adding a runtime-specific signal to help incident-bot auto-suggest a taxonomy category.
Thread reviewing a postmortem draft where runtime was blamed; discussion about correct owner vs contributing factor.
Thread from Support asking how to communicate incident type to a Dedicated customer and whether remediation SLA applies.
Thread linking a set of SUP tickets and proposing they map to a single taxonomy category; request for SRE validation.
Thread coordinating a customer escalation where incident type was initially misclassified; follow-up on updating the decision tree.
Thread about updating the postmortem template: required taxonomy fields, how to handle 'unknown', and who reviews classification accuracy.
Thread reviewing first week of postmortems using taxonomy; list of confusing categories and proposed tweaks for v1.1.
Working doc summarizing incident review data: counts by symptom, rough clustering, candidate taxonomy categories, and notes on data quality gaps.
Informal brainstorm notes: alternate category names, pros/cons, unresolved questions, and examples pulled from recent incidents.
Draft decision tree for on-call classification with quick checks (5xx vs latency vs streaming vs auth vs capacity) and links to dashboards.
Draft proposal from Observability: metric schema changes, label allowlist, sampling strategy, and an impact estimate on storage/cardinality.
Draft schema for owner mapping in control plane (type/subtype -> owner, secondary, runbook links), including validation rules and rollout notes.
Fleet team notes linking capacity signals (GPU saturation, provisioning lag, regional constraints) to taxonomy categories and suggested mitigations.
Product ops working doc evaluating remediation SLA options by tier and severity, including where commitments differ for Dedicated/Private.
Workshop notes with attendee list, decisions made live, parking lot items, and follow-up actions assigned to owners.
Draft customer comms snippets by incident type (what we can say, what to avoid), plus mapping to CS escalation steps.
Spreadsheet-style doc: list of historical incidents/support escalations with proposed taxonomy classification, owner, confidence score, and notes.
Customer support ticket capturing intermittent 500s and elevated latency during a failover event; includes logs, timeline, and links to incident channel used to validate taxonomy mapping.
Support ticket about streaming disconnect spikes after a client SDK upgrade; used as an example for classification boundaries (client vs gateway vs runtime).
Dedicated customer escalates 429s during burst; investigation distinguishes quota enforcement vs capacity saturation; includes proposed taxonomy classification.
Latency regression tied to a model rollout; links to canary signals and a hotfix PR; used to define 'rollout regression' subtype and owner.
Private deployment connectivity errors after upgrade (DNS/TLS); helps validate private-deployment incident categories and ownership split (Infra vs Private Deployments).
Enterprise customer cannot update routing policies due to control plane errors; includes impact assessment and drives owner mapping for control plane incidents.
Internal support ticket: incident-bot Slack modal missing required taxonomy fields for some users/workspaces; coordination between SRE and tooling owners.
Internal helpdesk ticket: CS cannot access incident taxonomy dashboards due to permissions; used to refine access model and comms workflow.
Internal recorded working session transcript: walking through proposed taxonomy, debating tricky incidents, and assigning owners for disputed categories.
Customer post-incident review call transcript (Dedicated): recap of incident type, mitigations, customer concerns, and action items; used to validate comms templates and SLA expectations.
Customer call transcript focused on overload/graceful degradation behavior and how remediation SLAs will be communicated and tracked for Dedicated customers.
Email thread coordinating cross-team review/signoff for taxonomy v1 (SRE, Platform, Infra, Runtime), with open questions and a target rollout date.
Leadership email thread requesting approval for remediation SLAs and escalation policy, including risk notes and expected operational impact.
Email thread resolving an ownership dispute for capacity-related incident subtypes; includes final decision, rationale, and follow-up action items.
Product/Eng email thread about how incident type will appear in Console and what CS can access; includes permissioning and rollout comms.
Email thread between Product Dedicated, CS, and SRE aligning dedicated-tier remediation SLAs and standard customer communication language.
